title: Reaction rate and energy - 123 school
heading: Reaction rate and energy
intro: You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.question: What is an exothermic reaction?

answers.a: A reaction in which a gas is formed
answers.b: A reaction in which energy is needed
answers.c: A reaction that proceeds very quickly
answers.d: A reaction in which energy is released

questions.question: What is an endothermic reaction?

answers.a: A reaction in which energy is absorbed
answers.b: A reaction without an energy effect
answers.c: A reaction in which energy is released
answers.d: A reaction in which a precipitate is formed

questions.question: Is the combustion of natural gas exothermic or endothermic?
Is photosynthesis exothermic or endothermic?
What is the activation energy?

answers.b: The energy supplied by the catalyst
answers.c: The energy released in the reaction
answers.d: The minimum energy needed to start a reaction

questions.question: What is a catalyst?

answers.a: A substance that is converted in the reaction
answers.b: A substance that slows down a reaction
answers.c: A substance that speeds up a reaction and is not used up itself

questions.question: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy?
What does a catalyst do to the heat of reaction?

answers.a: Nothing, the heat of reaction stays the same

questions.question: What is an effective collision?

answers.a: A collision with the wall of the vessel
answers.c: A collision between particles of the same substance
answers.d: A collision between particles with enough energy and in the right orientation, after which they react

questions.question: Why does a reaction go faster at a higher temperature?

answers.b: The particles move faster, so there are more effective collisions per second

questions.question: Why does a reaction go faster at a higher concentration?

answers.c: There are more particles per volume, so more collisions per second

questions.question: Why does zinc powder react faster with hydrochloric acid than a piece of zinc of the same mass?

answers.b: Powder has a larger contact surface
answers.c: Powder has a lower activation energy

questions.question: What happens to the reaction rate of gases if you increase the pressure?

answers.b: The rate becomes greater, because there are more particles per volume

questions.question: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. What happens to the rate for a 20 °C rise?
According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 20 °C a reaction takes 80 s. How long does the reaction take at 40 °C?
According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 50 °C a reaction takes 12 s. How long does the reaction take at 30 °C?
According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 20 °C a reaction takes 100 s. How long does the reaction take at 30 °C?
According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. How many times as great is the rate at 50 °C as at 20 °C?
According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 60 °C a reaction takes 5 s. How long does the reaction take at 20 °C?
How is the reaction rate defined?

answers.a: The amount of energy per mole
answers.c: The change in concentration per time (Δc : Δt)

questions.question: What is a suitable unit for reaction rate?
The concentration of substance A falls from 0.80 mol/L to 0.50 mol/L in 30 s. Calculate the average reaction rate.
In a reaction, 12 mL of gas is formed in 40 s. Calculate the average reaction rate in mL/s.

In an energy diagram of an exothermic reaction, where is the level of the products?

answers.a: Equal to the level of the reactants
answers.b: Lower than the level of the reactants
answers.d: Higher than the level of the reactants

questions.question: In an energy diagram of an endothermic reaction, where is the level of the products?

answers.a: Lower than the level of the reactants
answers.b: Higher than the level of the reactants
answers.d: Equal to the level of the reactants

questions.question: How do you read the heat of reaction from an energy diagram?

answers.a: The difference in height between the top and the products
answers.b: The height of the top of the hill
answers.c: The difference in height between the level of the reactants and that of the products

What is a dynamic equilibrium?

answers.b: The forward reaction and the reverse reaction proceed at the same rate
answers.c: Only the forward reaction takes place
